newsitem.title: POLAND: NEW POLISH RATING AGENCY READY TO EVALUATE ISSUERS.
newsitem.headline: NEW POLISH RATING AGENCY READY TO EVALUATE ISSUERS.

text.p: The newly founded Warsaw-based Central European Centre of Rating and Research (CERA) is already in talks with first issuers interested in services of the first rating agency in the region, CERA president said on Wednesday.

Wojciech Lipka told a news conference the agency would initially focus on evaluating the risk of investment in Polish debt securities but was also prepared to cover issuers from other central and eastern European countries.
"We are ready to accept applications for ratings from banks, companies and municipalities," Lipka said.
"We are already holding talks with potential issuers," he added.
Lipka said the agency would apply similar methods and procedures as well-established agencies: Moody's, Standard & Poor's and IBCA.
It has introduced nine basic categories ranging from "AAA" for the top investment grade to most risky "C" with possible additional sub-categories.
The Polish agency, which has 17 shareholders, mainly banks and share capital of 1.465 million zlotys, was registered a month ago after a year of preparations.
Its fees will depend on the issue size but will not exceed 30,000 zlotys for minicipal issues and 50,000 zlotys for banks and corporates, Lipka said.
